attempted_axis: Run-43 TOOL lane: 10 amendment items against tools/gdl + memory_graph, each symptom REPRODUCED before any fix, each discriminant DERIVED rather than taken from the item's framing, and each new gate/classifier/convention CALIBRATED against the live corpus. One commit per item, scoped tests between items, full suites per commit, ninja green at close.

attributes.law_screen: Screened claim.law.MT_a-banked-in-the-graph-premise-is-not-a-citation (item 3's queue text cites 'NM run-42' with no record id; `gdlmem search` returns only the work_claim itself, so the premise was measured rather than trusted). Screened the AGENTS.md run-39/41 calibration rule (calibrate every new gate/classifier against the live corpus before shipping) and applied it to items 1, 2, 5 and 10. Screened AGENTS.md rule 17 (promotion damage) and applied it in items 9 and in promoting this lane's two census tools. Screened AGENTS.md discipline 15 (no python -c; commit messages via -F) and followed it throughout. No codegen law applies: this lane changed no C source and no score.
attributes.residual: ITEM 1, graph-suite --changed: MEASURED the suite's real input set by instrumenting builtins.open/os.stat/os.scandir over a full run (2,164 repo paths, 336 tests, 0 failures) instead of assuming the item's 'no memory_graph file' framing. Four roots: memory_graph/, tools/gdl/, config/GUNE5D/, research/xbox_symbols/. Nothing under src/, include/, configure.py or AGENTS.md is read at all. Calibrated over 60 main commits: the sound gate skips 30 (50%, ~20 min); the naive reading would skip 47 and 17 of those would be WRONG (every tools/gdl source is a graph build input, and config/GUNE5D/webfrank.json feeds law_corpus pin queries). Skip path 0.59s vs 40.9s = 40.3s saved per skipped commit. Falsifier shipped: tools/gdl/composed_census/t13_suite_inputs.py re-measures, and test_every_core_build_input_is_relevant fails if core grows an input class outside the four roots. ITEM 2, CQ/CR dedup: the merged core is fndiff.datum_screen_from_lines / datum_multiset_screen (CR's calibrated suppressions + CQ's raw-object selection), exposed as `fndiff --datum [--raw] [--resolve-lbl]`. cr_datum_screen delegates and reproduces its --image census BYTE-IDENTICALLY over all 1,702 screened functions (VALUE-DELTA=49, VALUE-EQUAL=1653). cq_raw_pool_screen keeps its pipeline and shares the readers; verified byte-identical on 55 live functions. PREMISE PARTLY REFUTED: the two tools are not two halves of one screen, they answer different questions — CQ resolves POOL data only and drops every other relocation, CR keys every relocation; over 55 functions the verdicts disagree 28 times, always CQ=VALUE-EQUAL vs CR=VALUE-DELTA. NEW CALIBRATION FOUND: CR calls our `extern u8 lbl_8023D000[]` placeholder a different datum from the splitter's name for that address (retail `atree_scroll`); `--resolve-lbl` folds them, removing one whole false-positive function (pb_diag::pbDiagDrawInfo, 4 rows), re-keying 3 rows and adding no new delta. OFF by default so CE's lane keeps the verdicts it started with — recommend flipping the default at merge. Also stale: all five of CR's shipped calibration controls now read VALUE-EQUAL because run 42 FIXED those defects. ITEM 3, nearmiss dropped row: REFUTED as stated. An independent enumeration from report.json finds 221 functions in the >=90 band and nearmiss prints 221 — no row is lost in the report path. The real mechanism is `--parked skip`, which hides 142 of the 221 (99.97% MBCameraUpdate, 99.05% do_enemy_move among them) and said nothing, while the footer counted only what it printed and cited a PARKED.txt the tool has not read since the parks moved into the graph. Both halves are now stated, and every row carries rec=N (its attempt-record count) so the AGENTS close-lane screen 'rank by records-per-unmatched-function' no longer has to be reconstructed by hand. ITEM 4, probe --revert-best: the rolling snapshot follows the LAST banking verdict (NEUTRAL banks too), so the best-scoring bytes stop being reachable as soon as anything else banks. probe now writes a reserved `__best` bank whenever the BEST anchor moves onto the bytes just probed, keyed on the object DIGEST (a NEUTRAL that ties `real` must not overwrite it), and --revert-best restores it through the ordinary restore path (stale-restore guard, function scoping, transient-pin restore, re-score). Exercised live on game/mb/mb_camera::MBCameraUpdate. ITEM 5, hypothesis vs the record's own denial: the queue item's stated cause ('the screen pairs against cited records only') is WRONG — Gate J already flattens the record's own text. The measured defect is precision drift: 5 live firings, 4 false. Three were law-screen sentences ('claim.law.X SCREENED and NOT applicable here - it does NOT reach ...'), one of which flagged a record for AGREEING with itself; the fourth was a path-vs-basename double count ({game/mb/mb_model, mb_model}). Two narrowings take it to 1 of 1 with the true positive intact. The item's EXTENSION is REFUTED: pairing the typed denial.scope directly with the mandate fires on 18 of the 43 records carrying both (42%), and every example read is legitimate — a denial scoped to 'axis A on function F ONLY' and a hypothesis mandating 'run tool T on function F' share the subject by construction. ITEM 6, arbitration flags: PARTLY REFUTED — there are three things, not two. probe's --arbitrate is a MEASUREMENT (builds both states, prints both (real, fuzzy) pairs, banks nothing) while defake_gate's --arbitrate is the DECISION that accepts a CONFLICT. Aliasing them would have been wrong; defake_gate now also accepts probe's accept word --rebase-best, probe's readout header states the collision, and an accepted CONFLICT prints as ARBITRATED instead of repeating '(pass --arbitrate to accept)' above 'GATE OK (arbitrated)'. ITEM 7: both traps reproduced and added to AGENTS first-five-minutes. `python tools/gdl/nearmiss.py --min 90 | Select-Object -First 2; $LASTEXITCODE` = -1 while -Last = 0, and it is INTERMITTENT (a command that finishes writing first exits 0). `'OK|FAILED' -SimpleMatch` matches 0 lines where the regex matches 2. ITEM 8: 18 census tools take a unit and 16 did not normalize, so the core tools' `game/x/y.c` spelling produced `...y.c.o` and a MISSING OBJECT. fndiff.unit_key is now the one normalizer; cn_analyze.our_object/target_object is the choke point that fixes 11 tools (the whole WR family, ch_derive, ha_close, hv_perm/rctrace/repair, wf_word_diff) and cn_derive/cv_probe/wf_enumerate_orders/wf_detail were patched directly. Verified: wf_word_diff and cr_datum_screen give identical output for both spellings. ITEM 9: wf_dump was one of SIX files carrying the identical rule-17 damage (ROOT = HERE/'..' then sys.path.insert(ROOT/'tools/gdl') = tools/gdl/tools/gdl): wf_detail, wf_dump, wf_dcs_screen, wf_recolor_probe, wf_sim, wf_web, every one dead with ModuleNotFoundError from any directory. All six repaired and RUN; test_promotion_paths.py computes where each file's insert lands and fails if the directory does not exist. ITEM 10: measured all 62 tools/gdl modules by importing each in a fresh subprocess with a bare argv — 51 import silently, 9 do work at import (abicheck, build_rule, the addr16/addrlo/add_remat census family), 2 fail outright (pdb20_dump, splice_rules). The property is nearly universal, so the gap was DISCOVERABILITY: the `IMPORTABLE CORE:` docstring line now names the callable core of fndiff, slotdiff, savedregs, defake_gate and nearmiss, and test_importable_core.py fails if a marked module stops importing silently or renames a function it advertises.

hypothesis.cheapest_refuting_observation: Run `python tools/gdl/composed_census/cr_datum_screen.py --image --out build/GUNE5D/cr_after.txt` and diff it against a --resolve-lbl run: if the flag ever REMOVES a row whose two sides hold different bytes, or ADDS a delta, the recommendation is dead. For the second half, count the VALUE-DELTA rows whose target key starts `A:` and whose ours key starts `N:` — if that count is small, the UNDECIDED class is not worth a code change.
hypothesis.screened_against_target: no - the placeholder half is fully measured against the live objects (1,702 functions, before/after image census) but the byteless A:-vs-N: half was only counted by eye on the 49-row delta list; it has not been screened against the target bytes of any individual function.
hypothesis.statement: `fndiff --datum --resolve-lbl` should become the DEFAULT once CE's lane closes: on the live image it removes a whole false-positive function and 4 of the 49 VALUE-DELTA rows and adds nothing. The second, larger calibration debt it exposes is the got_it / HealthMeterFG / gNodeStackTop shape — our object defines a static whose address the splitter named lbl_ADDR, and the screen keys ours by NAME and retail by ADDRESS, so the row reads VALUE-DELTA with no value ever compared. Neither side has readable bytes there, so the correct verdict is UNDECIDED, not DELTA.
